text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- Yugoslav parliament to endorse the candidacy of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic for Yugoslav president. The parliament's mandate committees found Milosevic's candidacy the only valid one and rejected five others.
- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic and Serb member in Bosnia's multi-ethnic presidency Momcilo Krajisnik failed to bring their stands closer in a meeting held in Banja Luka.

- Bosnian Serb army commander General Pero Colic said new SFOR operations similar to the one that led to the murder and arrest of two Bosnian Serbs would mean an end to the implementation of the Dayton peace agreement.
- Defense attorney of Bosnian Serb Dusko Tadic said he would appeal the 20 year prison sentence passed by the International War Crimes Tribunal.
- Federal ministry for telecommunications shut down seven private radio stations without valid licences in Cacak, Serbia.
POLITIKA

- The Serbian parliament adopted in principle the law on financing of political parties; it continues Tuesday discussion on bill on electoral units to which the opposition has submitted almost 2,000 amendments.

- Travel through Yugoslavia is completely safe and not a single person was attacked on a train crossing the country, said Serbian Transport Minister Svetolik Kostadinovic in reaction to a warning by British travel agency Thomas Cook.
- Surface coal mines Kosovo, Dobro selo and Belacevac have produced 4.1 million tonnes of coal in the first six months this year which is 0.4 percent above plan.

- Yugoslavia to export fruits and vegetables to the value of $164 by end of year while $52 million were exported in the first six months, said director of Yugoslav fruit and vegetable fund Jovo Djilas.
- Banks are expected to start extending loans for primary agricultural production by end of year, said Yugoslav Agriculture Minister Nedeljko Sipovac.
- Swelling of river Danube not expected to cause any serious floods in Yugoslavia, says official of Yugoslav hydrometeorology institute.
- Municipal councillors of ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) and Yugoslav Left (JUL) to launch initative for replacement of Belgrade mayor Zoran Djindjic of the Democratic Party.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- Decisions of the group of deputies of the Montenegrin Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) supporting prime minister Milo Djukanovic are contrary to the party statute and to ethics, says Yugoslav justice minister and member of DPS main board Zoran Knezevic.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- The U.S. wants Kosovo Albanians to participate in Serbian elections and talks are under way between Kosovo Albanian leaders and Serbian opposition, according to the paper's source.

- Former president of the self-proclaimed Republic of Serb Krajina in Croatia Milan Martic fears he is next on the SFOR arrest list of war crimes suspects and changes his place of residence every night, according to his bodyguards.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Russia's Aeroflot to fly once a week on Mondays from Moscow to Tivat on the Montenegrin coast until October 27.
- "I found out that my name is on secret SFOR lists too," says Bosnian Serb Army Chief of General Staff General Pero Colic commenting arrests of war crimes suspects in Bosnia.

- After failed attempt to proclaim Moslem autonomy in Sandzak region, tensions ease in Novi Pazar. Sandzak Moslem National Council leader Sulejman Ugljanin persists in goals of "Bosniak people", announces dialogue with Yugoslav authorities.
- After six years, Croatian customs officials posted on border crossings in Ilok, Bogojevo, Batina and Tovarnik, between Srem-Baranja region in Croatia and Yugoslavia.
- Frequent rains in July slow down wheat harvest in Serbia.
BORBA
- Yumco textile factory plans to export $60 million this year, annual production worth over $200 million.
DANAS
- Kosovo Albanians will not vote in Serbian presidential elections, says Parliamentary Party of Kosova.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and Serbian Radical Party leader Vojislav Seselj most trusted politicians, according to a poll conducted by Mark-Plan agency.

- The minus in Serbia's pension fund will continue growing to the year 2010. Around 400 million German marks needed per month to pay out pensions, half of which is secured through taxes on wages of employed while half is lacking, says Economics Institute analyst Zoran Popov.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- Municipal boards of ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) in Bijelo Polje and Pljevlja declare as illegitimate decisions of the DPS main board at sessions not chaired by party president Momir Bulatovic and expel members who participated in the decision making. Budva and Tivat DPS municipal boards support the main board decision.
- The DPS main board cancelled all decisions of its municipal committees in Podgorica and Pljevlja and disbanded the committes over violation of the statute. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
